### Write functions to determine differences

First, evaluate_group_sizes() is a diagnostic to determine if difference tests can be run. 

Similarly, summarize_group_sizes() will output the number of observations for each group.

The differences() function will:
- Filter out groups with <2 observations
- Use shapiro.test() on ANOVA residuals to test the normality of the distribution, and output to "Distribution" whether the residual distribution is normal (P>0.05), has minor non-normality (W>0.9 but P<0.05), or has major non-normality (W<0.9, P<0.01)
- Use bartlett.test() if residuals are normally distributed or leveneTest() if not to test for homogeneity of variance in the data, and output to "Variance" whether the variance is homogeneous (P>0.05) or heterogeneous (P<0.05)
- If data meet parametric assumptions (normal distribution or minor non-normality, and homogeneity of variance), then procede with one-way ANOVA and Tukey's HSD post hoc test, or otherwise (major non-normality and/or heterogeneity of variance), use Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's Test
- Output tests used, P-values for the post hoc tests, and significance level indicators for a quick look
- Tell which factor group has a higher mean (if parametric) or median (non-parametric) value for the continuous variable in a Comparison column

The differences_multifactor() function will accept a vector of factors (1-3) and runs the same tests as differences() with these differences: 
- Uses a model formula to assess all factors and interactions
- Uses two-way or three-way ANOVA for parametric data, and Aligned Ranks Transformation (ART) ANOVA for non-parametric

Uses car, lme4, emmeans, and ARTool packages.


```{r set up group size functions}

#pairwise comparisons

#first look at group sizes
evaluate_group_sizes <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars) {
  insufficient_groups <- list()

  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    for (factor in factors) {
      filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, c(factor, cont_var)]) #remove NA values for continuous variable and factor

      #drop unused factor levels
      if (is.factor(filtered_data[[factor]])) {
        filtered_data[[factor]] <- droplevels(filtered_data[[factor]])
      }

      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]]) #calculate group sizes
      
      #identify groups with fewer than 2 observations
      insufficient <- group_sizes[group_sizes < 2]
      if (length(insufficient) > 0) {
        insufficient_groups[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
          Factor = factor,
          Continuous_Var = cont_var,
          Group = names(insufficient),
          Observations = as.numeric(insufficient)
        )
      }
    }
  }

  #combine results into a single dataframe
  if (length(insufficient_groups) > 0) {
    return(bind_rows(insufficient_groups, .id = "Combination"))
  } else {
    return(data.frame(
      Combination = character(),
      Factor = character(),
      Continuous_Var = character(),
      Group = character(),
      Observations = numeric()
    ))
  }
}

summarize_group_sizes <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars) {
  group_summary <- list()
  
  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    for (factor in factors) {
      filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, c(factor, cont_var)])
      
      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]])
      
      group_summary[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
        Continuous_Var = cont_var,
        Factor = factor,
        Group = names(group_sizes),
        Observations = as.numeric(group_sizes)
      )
    }
  }
  
  return(bind_rows(group_summary))
}

#analysis function with Shapiro test, Levene test, Bartlett's test, group size evaluation, and NA omission
differences <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars) {
  results_list <- list()

  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    for (factor in factors) {
      #remove NA values for the current continuous variable and factor
      filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, c(factor, cont_var)])

      #check if all groups for the factor have at least 2 observations
      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]])
      if (any(group_sizes < 2)) {
        #if a group has fewer than 2 observations, skip analysis and add a note
        results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
          Comparison = NA,
          Factor = factor,
          Continuous_Var = cont_var,
          Distribution = "Skipped",
          Variance = "Skipped",
          Test = "Skipped (Insufficient group size)",
          P_Value = NA,
          Significance = "Not significant"
        )
        next
      }

      #step 1: test normality using Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals
      anova_res <- aov(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
      residuals <- residuals(anova_res)
      shapiro <- shapiro.test(residuals)
      
      #determine normality category
      if (shapiro$p.value > 0.05) {
        distribution_status <- "Normal"
      } else if (shapiro$statistic > 0.9) {
        distribution_status <- "Minor non-normality"
      } else {
        distribution_status <- "Major non-normality"
      }

      #step 2: test homogeneity of variances
      #use Bartlett's test if normally distributed, Levene's test if not
      if (distribution_status == "Normal") {
        bartlett <- bartlett.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
        variance_test_pvalue <- bartlett$p.value
        variance_test_name <- "Bartlett"
      } else {
        levene <- car::leveneTest(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
        variance_test_pvalue <- levene$`Pr(>F)`[1]
        variance_test_name <- "Levene"
      }
      
      #determine homogeneity status
      variance_status <- ifelse(variance_test_pvalue > 0.05, "Homogeneous", "Heterogeneous")

      #step 3: decide which statistical test to use based on parametric assumptions
      #parametric assumptions met: normal distribution (or minor non-normality) AND homogeneous variances
      use_parametric <- (distribution_status %in% c("Normal", "Minor non-normality")) && (variance_status == "Homogeneous")

      if (use_parametric) {
        #ANOVA and Tukey's HSD
        tukey <- TukeyHSD(anova_res)

        #extract pairwise comparisons and P-values
        if (!is.null(tukey[[1]])) {
          #calculate group means for ordering comparisons
          group_means <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- rownames(tukey[[1]])
          p_values <- tukey[[1]][, "p adj"]
          
          #reorder comparisons so higher mean is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, "-")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_means[group1] > group_means[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Tukey's HSD (ANOVA)",
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          )

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          #if no valid groupings are present, return an empty dataframe
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Tukey's HSD (No significant groupings)",
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      } else {
        #Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's Test for non-parametric data
        kruskal <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)

        if (kruskal$p.value < 0.05) { #Dunn's Test if Kruskal-Wallis is significant
          dunn <- dunn.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], method = "bonferroni", kw = FALSE)

          #calculate group medians for ordering comparisons
          group_medians <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], median, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- dunn$comparisons
          p_values <- dunn$P.adjusted
          
          #reorder comparisons so higher median is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, " - ")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_medians[group1] > group_medians[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Dunn's Test (Kruskal-Wallis)",
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          ) %>%
            filter(P_Value < 1)

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Kruskal-Wallis (NS)",
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  #combine results for all factors and continuous variables
  results_df <- bind_rows(results_list, .id = "Analysis_Combination")
  
  return(results_df)
}

#analysis function for multifactor models with Shapiro test, Levene test, Bartlett's test, group size evaluation, and NA omission
differences_multifactor <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars) {
  results_list <- list()

  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    # Create formula with all factors
    factor_formula <- paste(factors, collapse = " * ")
    full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula))
    
    # Remove NA values for the current continuous variable and all factors
    cols_needed <- c(factors, cont_var)
    filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, cols_needed])

    # Check if all groups for each factor have at least 2 observations
    insufficient_groups <- FALSE
    for (factor in factors) {
      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]])
      if (any(group_sizes < 2)) {
        insufficient_groups <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
    
    if (insufficient_groups) {
      # If any factor has groups with fewer than 2 observations, skip analysis and add a note
      results_list[[cont_var]] <- data.frame(
        Comparison = NA,
        Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
        Continuous_Var = cont_var,
        Distribution = "Skipped",
        Variance = "Skipped",
        Test = "Skipped (Insufficient group size)",
        P_Value = NA,
        Significance = "Not significant"
      )
      next
    }

    # Step 1: Test normality using Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals
    anova_res <- aov(full_formula, data = filtered_data)
    residuals <- residuals(anova_res)
    shapiro <- shapiro.test(residuals)
    
    # Determine normality category
    if (shapiro$p.value > 0.05) {
      distribution_status <- "Normal"
    } else if (shapiro$statistic > 0.9) {
      distribution_status <- "Minor non-normality"
    } else {
      distribution_status <- "Major non-normality"
    }

    # Step 2: Test homogeneity of variances
    # Create interaction groups for both Bartlett and Levene tests
    if (length(factors) == 1) {
      interaction_groups <- filtered_data[[factors[1]]]
    } else if (length(factors) == 2) {
      interaction_groups <- interaction(filtered_data[[factors[1]]], filtered_data[[factors[2]]])
    } else if (length(factors) == 3) {
      interaction_groups <- interaction(filtered_data[[factors[1]]], filtered_data[[factors[2]]], filtered_data[[factors[3]]])
    }
    
    # Use Bartlett's test if normally distributed, Levene's test if not
    if (distribution_status == "Normal") {
      bartlett <- bartlett.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], interaction_groups)
      variance_test_pvalue <- bartlett$p.value
    } else {
      levene <- car::leveneTest(filtered_data[[cont_var]], interaction_groups)
      variance_test_pvalue <- levene$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    }

    # Step 3: Decide which statistical test to use
    # Parametric assumptions met: Normal distribution (or minor non-normality) AND homogeneous variances
    use_parametric <- (distribution_status %in% c("Normal", "Minor non-normality")) && (variance_status == "Homogeneous")

    if (use_parametric) {
      # ANOVA and Tukey's HSD
      tukey <- TukeyHSD(anova_res)

      # Extract pairwise comparisons and P-values for each factor
      for (i in seq_along(tukey)) {
        factor_name <- names(tukey)[i]
        
        if (!is.null(tukey[[i]])) {
          # Calculate group means for ordering comparisons
          group_means <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor_name]], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- rownames(tukey[[i]])
          p_values <- tukey[[i]][, "p adj"]
          
          # Reorder comparisons so higher mean is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, "-")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_means[group1] > group_means[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Tukey's HSD (ANOVA) -", factor_name),
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          )

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor_name, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's Test for each factor
      for (factor in factors) {
        kruskal <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)

        if (kruskal$p.value < 0.05) { # Dunn's Test if Kruskal-Wallis is significant
          dunn <- dunn.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], method = "bonferroni", kw = FALSE)

          # Calculate group medians for ordering comparisons
          group_medians <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], median, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- dunn$comparisons
          p_values <- dunn$P.adjusted
          
          # Reorder comparisons so higher median is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, " - ")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_medians[group1] > group_medians[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Dunn's Test (Kruskal-Wallis) -", factor),
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          ) %>%
            filter(P_Value < 1)

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Kruskal-Wallis (NS) -", factor),
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  # Combine results for all factors and continuous variables
  results_df <- bind_rows(results_list, .id = "Analysis_Combination")
  
  return(results_df)
}
```

```{r set up one-way pairwise comparison function}

#pairwise comparisons

#analysis function with Shapiro test, Levene test, Bartlett's test, group size evaluation, and NA omission
differences <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars) {
  results_list <- list()

  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    for (factor in factors) {
      #remove NA values for the current continuous variable and factor
      filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, c(factor, cont_var)])

      #check if all groups for the factor have at least 2 observations
      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]])
      if (any(group_sizes < 2)) {
        #if a group has fewer than 2 observations, skip analysis and add a note
        results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
          Comparison = NA,
          Factor = factor,
          Continuous_Var = cont_var,
          Distribution = "Skipped",
          Variance = "Skipped",
          Test = "Skipped (Insufficient group size)",
          P_Value = NA,
          Significance = "Not significant"
        )
        next
      }

      #step 1: test normality using Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals
      anova_res <- aov(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
      residuals <- residuals(anova_res)
      shapiro <- shapiro.test(residuals)
      
      #determine normality category
      if (shapiro$p.value > 0.05) {
        distribution_status <- "Normal"
      } else if (shapiro$statistic > 0.9) {
        distribution_status <- "Minor non-normality"
      } else {
        distribution_status <- "Major non-normality"
      }

      #step 2: test homogeneity of variances
      #use Bartlett's test if normally distributed, Levene's test if not
      if (distribution_status == "Normal") {
        bartlett <- bartlett.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
        variance_test_pvalue <- bartlett$p.value
        variance_test_name <- "Bartlett"
      } else {
        levene <- car::leveneTest(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)
        variance_test_pvalue <- levene$`Pr(>F)`[1]
        variance_test_name <- "Levene"
      }
      
      #determine homogeneity status
      variance_status <- ifelse(variance_test_pvalue > 0.05, "Homogeneous", "Heterogeneous")

      #step 3: decide which statistical test to use based on parametric assumptions
      #parametric assumptions met: normal distribution (or minor non-normality) AND homogeneous variances
      use_parametric <- (distribution_status %in% c("Normal", "Minor non-normality")) && (variance_status == "Homogeneous")

      if (use_parametric) {
        #ANOVA and Tukey's HSD
        tukey <- TukeyHSD(anova_res)

        #extract pairwise comparisons and P-values
        if (!is.null(tukey[[1]])) {
          #calculate group means for ordering comparisons
          group_means <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- rownames(tukey[[1]])
          p_values <- tukey[[1]][, "p adj"]
          
          #reorder comparisons so higher mean is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, "-")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_means[group1] > group_means[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Tukey's HSD (ANOVA)",
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          )

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          #if no valid groupings are present, return an empty dataframe
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Tukey's HSD (No significant groupings)",
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      } else {
        #Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's Test for non-parametric data
        kruskal <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)

        if (kruskal$p.value < 0.05) { #Dunn's Test if Kruskal-Wallis is significant
          dunn <- dunn.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], method = "bonferroni", kw = FALSE)

          #calculate group medians for ordering comparisons
          group_medians <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], median, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- dunn$comparisons
          p_values <- dunn$P.adjusted
          
          #reorder comparisons so higher median is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, " - ")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_medians[group1] > group_medians[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Dunn's Test (Kruskal-Wallis)",
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          ) %>%
            filter(P_Value < 1)

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factor = factor,
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = "Kruskal-Wallis (NS)",
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  #combine results for all factors and continuous variables
  results_df <- bind_rows(results_list, .id = "Analysis_Combination")
  
  return(results_df)
}
```

```{r set up multifactoral function}

#analysis function for multifactor models with interactions, Shapiro test, Levene test, Bartlett's test, group size evaluation, and NA omission
differences_multifactor <- function(data, factors, continuous_vars, random_var = NULL) {
  results_list <- list()

  for (cont_var in continuous_vars) {
    # Create formula with all factors and interactions
    factor_formula <- paste(factors, collapse = " * ")
    
    # Remove NA values for the current continuous variable and all factors
    cols_needed <- c(factors, cont_var)
    if (!is.null(random_var)) {
      cols_needed <- c(cols_needed, random_var)
    }
    filtered_data <- na.omit(data[, cols_needed])

    # Check if all groups for each factor have at least 2 observations
    insufficient_groups <- FALSE
    for (factor in factors) {
      group_sizes <- table(filtered_data[[factor]])
      if (any(group_sizes < 2)) {
        insufficient_groups <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
    
    if (insufficient_groups) {
      # If any factor has groups with fewer than 2 observations, skip analysis and add a note
      results_list[[cont_var]] <- data.frame(
        Comparison = NA,
        Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
        Continuous_Var = cont_var,
        Distribution = "Skipped",
        Variance = "Skipped",
        Test = "Skipped (Insufficient group size)",
        P_Value = NA,
        Significance = "Not significant"
      )
      next
    }

    # Step 1: Test normality using Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals
    if (is.null(random_var)) {
      full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula))
      anova_res <- aov(full_formula, data = filtered_data)
    } else {
      full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula, "+ (1|", random_var, ")"))
      anova_res <- lme4::lmer(full_formula, data = filtered_data, REML = TRUE, na.action = na.omit)
    }
    
    residuals <- residuals(anova_res)
    shapiro <- shapiro.test(residuals)
    
    # Determine normality category
    if (shapiro$p.value > 0.05) {
      distribution_status <- "Normal"
    } else if (shapiro$statistic > 0.9) {
      distribution_status <- "Minor non-normality"
    } else {
      distribution_status <- "Major non-normality"
    }

    # Step 2: Test homogeneity of variances
    # Create interaction groups for both Bartlett and Levene tests
    if (length(factors) == 1) {
      interaction_groups <- filtered_data[[factors[1]]]
    } else if (length(factors) == 2) {
      interaction_groups <- interaction(filtered_data[[factors[1]]], filtered_data[[factors[2]]])
    } else if (length(factors) == 3) {
      interaction_groups <- interaction(filtered_data[[factors[1]]], filtered_data[[factors[2]]], filtered_data[[factors[3]]])
    }
    
    # Use Bartlett's test if normally distributed, Levene's test if not
    if (distribution_status == "Normal") {
      bartlett <- bartlett.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], interaction_groups)
      variance_test_pvalue <- bartlett$p.value
    } else {
      levene <- car::leveneTest(filtered_data[[cont_var]], interaction_groups)
      variance_test_pvalue <- levene$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    }
    
    # Determine homogeneity status
    variance_status <- ifelse(variance_test_pvalue > 0.05, "Homogeneous", "Heterogeneous")

    # Step 3: Decide which statistical test to use
    # Parametric assumptions met: Normal distribution (or minor non-normality) AND homogeneous variances
    use_parametric <- (distribution_status %in% c("Normal", "Minor non-normality")) && (variance_status == "Homogeneous")

    if (use_parametric) {
      # Run Type III ANOVA
      if (is.null(random_var)) {
        full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula))
        lm_model <- lm(full_formula, data = filtered_data)
      } else {
        full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula, "+ (1|", random_var, ")"))
        lm_model <- lme4::lmer(full_formula, data = filtered_data, REML = TRUE, na.action = na.omit)
      }
      
      anova_results <- car::Anova(lm_model, type = 3)
      
      # Extract main effects and interactions from Type III ANOVA
      anova_df <- as.data.frame(anova_results)
      anova_df$Term <- rownames(anova_df)
      anova_df <- anova_df[!(rownames(anova_df) == "(Intercept)"), ] # Remove intercept
      
      for (idx in seq_len(nrow(anova_df))) {
        term_name <- anova_df$Term[idx]
        p_value <- anova_df$`Pr(>F)`[idx]
        
        sig_label <- case_when(
          p_value <= 0.001 ~ "***",
          p_value <= 0.01 ~ "**",
          p_value <= 0.05 ~ "*",
          TRUE ~ "Not significant"
        )
        
        results_list[[paste(cont_var, term_name, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
          Comparison = term_name,
          Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
          Continuous_Var = cont_var,
          Distribution = distribution_status,
          Variance = variance_status,
          Test = "Type III ANOVA",
          P_Value = p_value,
          Significance = sig_label
        )
      }
      
      # ANOVA and Tukey's HSD for pairwise comparisons
      if (is.null(random_var)) {
        full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula))
        anova_res <- aov(full_formula, data = filtered_data)
        tukey <- TukeyHSD(anova_res)
      } else {
        # For mixed models, use emmeans for post-hoc comparisons
        tukey_list <- list()
        for (factor in factors) {
          emmeans_result <- emmeans::emmeans(lm_model, as.formula(paste("~", factor)))
          tukey_list[[factor]] <- pairs(emmeans_result, adjust = "tukey")
        }
        tukey <- tukey_list
      }

      # Extract pairwise comparisons and P-values for each factor
      if (is.null(random_var)) {
        for (i in seq_along(tukey)) {
          factor_name <- names(tukey)[i]
          
          if (!is.null(tukey[[i]])) {
            # Calculate group means for ordering comparisons
            group_means <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor_name]], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
            
            comparisons <- rownames(tukey[[i]])
            p_values <- tukey[[i]][, "p adj"]
            
            # Reorder comparisons so higher mean is listed first
            reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
              groups <- strsplit(comp, "-")[[1]]
              group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
              group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
              
              if (group_means[group1] > group_means[group2]) {
                paste(group1, ">", group2)
              } else {
                paste(group2, ">", group1)
              }
            })
            
            sig_pairs <- data.frame(
              Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
              Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
              Continuous_Var = cont_var,
              Distribution = distribution_status,
              Variance = variance_status,
              Test = paste("Tukey's HSD -", factor_name),
              P_Value = p_values,
              Significance = case_when(
                p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
                p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
                p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
                TRUE ~ "Not significant"
              )
            )

            results_list[[paste(cont_var, "tukey", factor_name, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
          }
        }
      } else {
        # For mixed models with emmeans
        for (factor in factors) {
          tukey_result <- tukey[[factor]]
          p_values <- tukey_result@test$p.value
          comparisons <- as.character(tukey_result@grid$contrast)
          
          # Calculate group means for ordering comparisons
          group_means <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          # Reorder comparisons so higher mean is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, " - ")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_means[group1] > group_means[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Tukey's HSD -", factor),
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          )
          
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, "tukey", factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Run ART ANOVA for non-parametric
      # ARTool requires factors to be of class factor, not character
      art_data <- filtered_data
      for (factor in factors) {
        if (!is.factor(art_data[[factor]])) {
          art_data[[factor]] <- as.factor(art_data[[factor]])
        }
      }
      
      # Create the formula and run ART
      full_formula <- as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor_formula))
      art_result <- ARTool::art(full_formula, data = art_data)
      
      # Extract ART ANOVA results
      art_anova <- anova(art_result)
      art_df <- as.data.frame(art_anova)
      art_df$Term <- rownames(art_df)
      
      for (idx in seq_len(nrow(art_df))) {
        term_name <- art_df$Term[idx]
        p_value <- art_df$`Pr(>F)`[idx]
        
        sig_label <- case_when(
          p_value <= 0.001 ~ "***",
          p_value <= 0.01 ~ "**",
          p_value <= 0.05 ~ "*",
          TRUE ~ "Not significant"
        )
        
        results_list[[paste(cont_var, "art", term_name, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
          Comparison = term_name,
          Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
          Continuous_Var = cont_var,
          Distribution = distribution_status,
          Variance = variance_status,
          Test = "ART ANOVA",
          P_Value = p_value,
          Significance = sig_label
        )
      }
      
      # Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's Test for pairwise comparisons
      for (factor in factors) {
        kruskal <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(cont_var, "~", factor)), data = filtered_data)

        if (kruskal$p.value < 0.05) { # Dunn's Test if Kruskal-Wallis is significant
          dunn <- dunn.test(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], method = "bonferroni", kw = FALSE)

          # Calculate group medians for ordering comparisons
          group_medians <- tapply(filtered_data[[cont_var]], filtered_data[[factor]], median, na.rm = TRUE)
          
          comparisons <- dunn$comparisons
          p_values <- dunn$P.adjusted
          
          # Reorder comparisons so higher median is listed first
          reordered_comparisons <- sapply(comparisons, function(comp) {
            groups <- strsplit(comp, " - ")[[1]]
            group1 <- trimws(groups[1])
            group2 <- trimws(groups[2])
            
            if (group_medians[group1] > group_medians[group2]) {
              paste(group1, ">", group2)
            } else {
              paste(group2, ">", group1)
            }
          })
          
          sig_pairs <- data.frame(
            Comparison = reordered_comparisons,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Dunn's Test -", factor),
            P_Value = p_values,
            Significance = case_when(
              p_values <= 0.001 ~ "***",
              p_values <= 0.01 ~ "**",
              p_values <= 0.05 ~ "*",
              TRUE ~ "Not significant"
            )
          ) %>%
            filter(P_Value < 1)

          results_list[[paste(cont_var, "dunn", factor, sep = "_")]] <- sig_pairs
        } else {
          results_list[[paste(cont_var, "dunn", factor, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
            Comparison = NA,
            Factors = paste(factors, collapse = " * "),
            Continuous_Var = cont_var,
            Distribution = distribution_status,
            Variance = variance_status,
            Test = paste("Kruskal-Wallis (NS) -", factor),
            P_Value = NA,
            Significance = "Not significant"
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  # Combine results for all factors and continuous variables
  results_df <- bind_rows(results_list, .id = "Analysis_Combination")
  
  return(results_df)
}
```

```{r load coal calibration data}
#create chroma and hue function
add_ch <- function(df){
  df %>%
    mutate(
      chroma = sqrt(a^2 + b^2),
      hue = atan2(b, a) * 180 / pi  # degrees
    )
}
```

```{r load site data}
#read in site data

  group_by(Site_ID) %>%
    dplyr::select(!Mgmt_time) %>%
    dplyr::select(!Collar_Lat) %>%
```

### Plants

```{r load plant harvest data}

#read in 13C initial harvest data
harvest <- read_csv("Stagg_harvest.csv") %>% #load
  clean_names() #clean up column names

#pivot and calculate root:shoot ratio
plant_harvest <- harvest %>%
  mutate(across(c(8:17), as.numeric)) %>% #convert columns to numeric
  dplyr::select(site, site_id, management, pot, species, functional_group, sample_type, biomass_g) %>%
  filter(biomass_g >= 0) %>% #remove non-plant data
  group_by(site, site_id, management, pot, species, functional_group, sample_type) %>%
  summarise(biomass_g = mean(biomass_g, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>% #summarize duplicate entries for groups
  pivot_wider(names_from = sample_type, values_from = biomass_g) %>% #determines observation name and value columns
  mutate(root_shoot = #calculate root:shoot ratio
           case_when(root > 0 & shoot > 0 ~ root / shoot, #when values are present
                     TRUE ~ NA)) %>% #default to NA when values are not present
  mutate(harvesttime = #define harvest time
        case_when(pot == "G1" | pot == "G20" | pot == "G30" | pot == "G31" | pot == "G39" |
                  pot == "G8" | pot == "G33" | pot == "G35" | pot == "G41" | pot == "G42" |
                  pot == "G9" | pot == "G12" | pot == "G22" | pot == "GA1" | pot == "GA2" |
                  pot == "G11" | pot == "G18" | pot == "G29" | pot == "GF1" | pot == "GX"
                  ~ "T0", #time 0 beginning of incubation
                     TRUE ~ "T10mos")) #10 months incubation

#summarize biomass for plots
summary_harvest <- plant_harvest %>%
  dplyr::select(site, site_id, management, species, functional_group, shoot, root, root_shoot) %>%
  group_by(site, management, species, functional_group) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#summarize biomass by plant species for estimates
summary_species <- plant_harvest %>%
  dplyr::select(species, functional_group, shoot, root, root_shoot) %>%
  group_by(species, functional_group) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#13C calculations
nat_abun <- harvest %>%
  filter(grepl("pre", sample_type)) %>% #keep only pre-labelling data
  dplyr::select(site, site_id, sample_type, adjusted_delta, per_atom13c, per_c) %>%
  mutate(sample_type = str_replace(sample_type, "leaf pre sample", "shoot")) %>% #match naming
  mutate(sample_type = str_replace(sample_type, "root pre sample", "root")) %>% #match naming
  mutate(sample_type = str_replace(sample_type, "soil pre sample", "soil")) #match naming)

#13C df for plants only

plant13C <- harvest %>%
  filter(biomass_g >= 0) %>% #remove non-plant data
  dplyr::select(site, site_id, pot, species, functional_group, sample_type, biomass_g, adjusted_delta, per_atom13c, per_c) %>%
  mutate(total_c_mg = biomass_g * (per_c / 100) * 1000) %>% #calculate total C in mg
  mutate(excess_per13C = case_when(sample_type == "shoot" | sample_type == "root"
                     ~ per_atom13c - nat_abun$per_atom13c #calculate excess 13C
                     [match(paste(site, sample_type), 
                            paste(nat_abun$site, nat_abun$sample_type))], TRUE ~ NA)) %>% 
  mutate(excess13C_mg = case_when(sample_type == "shoot" | sample_type == "root"
                     ~ total_c_mg * (excess_per13C/100), #atom % times total C in mg
                     TRUE ~ NA)) 


#summarize means 13C for plots - by species
summary_plant13C_sp <- plant13C %>%
  group_by(site, site_id, sample_type, species, functional_group) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#sum 13C in shoots for plots - by pot
plant13C_shoots <- plant13C %>%
  filter(sample_type == "shoot") %>%
  dplyr::select(site, site_id, pot, biomass_g, total_c_mg, excess13C_mg) %>%
  group_by(site, site_id, pot) %>%
  summarise_all(funs(sum(., na.rm=TRUE)))#run all summary stats

#sum 13C in roots for plots - by pot
plant13C_roots <- plant13C %>%
  filter(sample_type == "root") %>%
  dplyr::select(site, site_id, pot, biomass_g, total_c_mg, excess13C_mg) %>%
  group_by(site, site_id, pot) %>%
  summarise_all(funs(sum(., na.rm=TRUE)))#run all summary stats

#summarize 13C for plots add up - by site and type only
summary_plant13C <- plant13C %>%
  dplyr::select(site, site_id, sample_type, pot, biomass_g, total_c_mg, excess13C_mg) %>%
  group_by(site, site_id, sample_type, pot) %>%
  summarise_all(funs(sum(., na.rm=TRUE))) %>% #first add up per pot
  group_by(site, site_id, sample_type) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats #then summarize per site

#add mean data to harvest data for estimates
plant_harvest_est <- plant_harvest %>%
  #replace(is.na(.), 0) %>%
  mutate(site2 =
           case_when(pot == "G20" | pot == "G31" | #higher root values
                       pot == "G37" | pot == "G7"
                     ~ "bickershaw1_high",
                     pot == "G1" | pot == "G30" | pot == "G39" | #lower root values
                       pot == "G34" | pot == "G26" | pot == "G3" 
                     ~ "bickershaw1_low",
                     pot == "G33" | pot == "G35" | pot == "G41" |
                       pot == "G23" | pot == "G24" |pot == "G40"
                     ~ "bickershaw2_high",
                     pot == "G8" | pot == "G42" |
                       pot == "G4" | pot == "G28"
                     ~ "bickershaw2_low",
                     pot == "G12" | pot == "GA1" | pot == "GA2" |
                       pot == "G5" | pot == "G6" | pot == "GA4" 
                     ~ "amberswood_high",
                     pot == "G22" | pot == "G9" |
                       pot == "G21" | pot == "GA3"
                     ~ "amberswood_low",
                     .default = site)) %>%
  mutate(root_shoot =
           case_when(root_shoot > 0 ~ root_shoot, 
                     TRUE ~ summary_species$root_shoot_mean
                     [match(species, summary_species$species)])) %>%
  mutate(root =
           case_when(root > 0 ~ root,
                     TRUE ~ root_shoot * shoot))
is.na(plant_harvest_est) <- sapply(plant_harvest_est, is.nan) #replace NaN with NA for better handling of missing data

#summarize general roots amount by site
general_roots <- plant_harvest_est %>%
  filter(species == "general_roots") %>%
  dplyr::select(site2, root) %>%
  group_by(site2) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#calculate and estimate biomass per pot
total_pots <- plant_harvest_est %>%
  dplyr::select(site_id, site2, management, pot, harvesttime, root, shoot, root_shoot) %>%
  group_by(site_id, site2, management, pot, harvesttime) %>%
  summarise(root = sum(root, na.rm=TRUE), shoot = sum(shoot, na.rm=TRUE), root_shoot = mean(root_shoot, na.rm=TRUE)) %>% #summarize
  mutate(root = #add some general roots to the estimated beginning biomass for incubation
           dplyr::case_when(harvesttime == "T0" ~ root,
                     TRUE ~ root + general_roots$root_mean[match(site2, general_roots$site2)])) #+
                     #general_roots$sd[match(site2, general_roots$site2)]))

#write csv for measured and estimated beginning biomass
#write.csv(plant_harvest_est, "begin_estimates_bysp.csv") #saves as csv in current workspace
#write.csv(total_pots, "begin_estimates_bypot.csv") #saves as csv in current workspace

#order variables
plant_harvest$site <- factor(plant_harvest$site, levels = order_sites)
plant_harvest$site_id <- factor(plant_harvest$site_id, levels = order_IDs)

plant_harvest_est$site_id <- factor(plant_harvest_est$site_id, levels = order_IDs)
```

```{r calc plant biodiversity}

#Pivot data to wide format
species_df_wide <- plant_harvest %>%
  dplyr::select(pot, species, shoot) %>% #select only needed columns
  filter(!is.na(species) & !grepl("general_roots", species)) %>% #remove any NA species
  pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = shoot) %>% #determines observation name and value columns
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% #make any missing values 0
  column_to_rownames(var="pot") #sets observation column as row names

#Calculate species richness, Shannon index, and Simpson index with vegan library
species_richness <- specnumber(species_df_wide) #calculate species richness
shannon <- diversity(species_df_wide, index = "shannon") #calculate Shannon index
simpson <- diversity(species_df_wide, index = "simpson") #calculate Simpson index

#Combine biodiversity metrics into a dataframe
diversity <- data.frame(
  pot = rownames(species_df_wide), #put observations back into column
  species_richness = species_richness,
  shannon = shannon,
  simpson = simpson,
  row.names = NULL
) 

diversity <- diversity %>%
  mutate(site_id = plant_harvest$site_id[match(diversity$pot, plant_harvest$pot)]) %>% #add site information back in
  mutate(site = plant_harvest$site[match(diversity$pot, plant_harvest$pot)])
```

```{r load AM and biomass fungi data}
#read in AM association data
AMdata <- read_csv("Wigan_myc.csv") 

#order variables
AMdata$Site <- factor(AMdata$Site, levels = order_sites)
AMdata$Mgmt_fct <- factor(AMdata$Mgmt_fct, levels = order_mgmt)
AMdata$Site_ID <- factor(AMdata$Site_ID, levels = order_IDs)

#read in HLD data
HLD <- read_csv("HLD_Wigan.csv")

#order variables
HLD$Site_ID <- factor(HLD$Site_ID, levels = order_IDs)

#calculate fungal biomass C
HLD <- HLD %>%
  mutate(other_biomass_gkg = other_sm_biomass_gkg + other_lg_biomass_gkg) %>%
  mutate(AM_C_mgkg = AM_mgkg * 0.3) %>% #use 30% C (Hodge and Fitter 2010, Zhang et al. 2025b), convert to mg per kg soil
  mutate(otherfun_mgkg = other_biomass_gkg * 1000) %>%
  mutate(otherfun_C_mgkg = otherfun_mgkg * 0.41) %>% #use 41% C (Pánek et al. 2024)
  mutate(total_fun_C_mgkg = AM_C_mgkg + otherfun_C_mgkg) #add together

#split timepoints
HLD_T0 <- HLD %>%
  filter(Timepoint == "T0") 

HLD_T6 <- HLD %>%
  filter(Timepoint == "T6") 

#melt to be able to stack a bar chart for biomass
fungal_mass <- HLD %>%
  dplyr::select(Site_ID, Pot, Timepoint, AM_biomass_gkg, other_biomass_gkg, total_fun_gkg) %>%
  pivot_longer(
		cols = c(AM_biomass_gkg, other_biomass_gkg, total_fun_gkg), #pick columns
		names_to = "fungal_type", #name column to put original column names in
		values_to = "g_biomass") #name column to put values in

#melt to be able to stack a bar chart for biomass C
fungal_C <- HLD %>%
  dplyr::select(Site_ID, Timepoint, AM_C_mgkg, otherfun_C_mgkg) %>%
  pivot_longer(
		cols = AM_C_mgkg:otherfun_C_mgkg, #pick columns
		names_to = "fungal_type", #name column to put original column names in
		values_to = "mg_C") #name column to put values in

#add % change in mass
fungal_chg <- fungal_mass %>%
  pivot_wider(
    #id_cols
		names_from = Timepoint, #name column to put original column names in
		values_from = g_biomass) %>% #name column to put values in
		#values_fn = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% #use mean of values
  mutate(diff_mg = (T6 - T0) * 1000)
```

```{r load process ITS, warning=FALSE}
  mutate(genus.species = paste(Genus, Species, sep = "."))
  
unique(taxa_ITS$genus.species)

sp.tf <- data.frame(genus.species=unique(taxa_ITS.sp$genus.species),

sp.tf #

#combine at species level

rownames(asv_ITS.s) <- rownames(asv_ITS)
colnames(asv_ITS.s) <- unique(taxa_ITS$genus.species)
for (i in 1:length(unique(taxa_ITS$genus.species))) {

  temp2 <- asv_ITS[, which(colnames(asv_ITS) %in% temp$asv), drop=FALSE]
  asv_ITS.s[,i] <- rowSums(temp2)
}
asv_ITS.s <- as.data.frame(asv_ITS.s) #make df



#alpha - species

}
env_ITS$sobs.s <- Reduce("+", its_sobs.list.s) / length(its_sobs.list.s)

#shannon
its_shannon.list.s <-  replicate(100, 1:dim(asv_ITS.s)[1], simplify = FALSE)
for (i in 1:100) {
  its_shannon.list.s[[i]] <- diversity(as.matrix(rrarefy(asv_ITS.s,sample=170)), index = "shannon")
}
env_ITS$shannon.s <- Reduce("+", its_shannon.list.s) / length(its_shannon.list.s)

#simpson
its_simpson.list.s <-  replicate(100, 1:dim(asv_ITS.s)[1], simplify = FALSE)
for (i in 1:100) {
  its_simpson.list.s[[i]] <- diversity(as.matrix(rrarefy(asv_ITS.s,sample=170)), index = "simpson")
}
env_ITS$simpson.s <- Reduce("+", its_simpson.list.s) / length(its_simpson.list.s)

#gini
its_gini.list.s <-  replicate(100, 1:dim(asv_ITS.s)[1], simplify = FALSE)
for (i in 1:100) {
  its_gini.list.s[[i]] <- apply(as.matrix(rrarefy(asv_ITS.s,sample=170)), 1, function(x) Gini(x))
}
env_ITS$gini.s <- Reduce("+", its_gini.list.s) / length(its_gini.list.s)


#combine at genus level
asv_ITS.g <- matrix(0, nrow=nrow(asv_ITS), ncol=length(unique(taxa_ITS$Genus)))
rownames(asv_ITS.g) <- rownames(asv_ITS)
colnames(asv_ITS.g) <- unique(taxa_ITS$Genus)
for (i in 1:length(unique(taxa_ITS$Genus))) {
  temp <- taxa_ITS[which(taxa_ITS$Genus == unique(taxa_ITS$Genus)[i]),]
  temp2 <- asv_ITS[, which(colnames(asv_ITS) %in% temp$asv), drop=FALSE]
  asv_ITS.g[,i] <- rowSums(temp2)
}
asv_ITS.g <- as.data.frame(asv_ITS.g)

#alpha - genus
#observed richness
its_sobs.list.g <-  replicate(1000, 1:dim(asv_ITS.g)[1], simplify = FALSE)
for (i in 1:1000) {
  its_sobs.list.g[[i]] <- specnumber(as.matrix(rrarefy(asv_ITS.g,sample=170)))
}
env_ITS$sobs.g <- Reduce("+", its_sobs.list.g) / length(its_sobs.list.g)

#shannon
its_shannon.list.g <-  replicate(100, 1:dim(asv_ITS.g)[1], simplify = FALSE)
for (i in 1:1000) {
  its_shannon.list.g[[i]] <- diversity(as.matrix(rrarefy(asv_ITS.g,sample=170)), index = "shannon")
}
env_ITS$shannon.g <- Reduce("+", its_shannon.list.g) / length(its_shannon.list.g)

#simpson
its_simpson.list.g <-  replicate(100, 1:dim(asv_ITS.g)[1], simplify = FALSE)
for (i in 1:100) {
  its_simpson.list.g[[i]] <- diversity(as.matrix(rrarefy(asv_ITS.g,sample=170)), index = "simpson")
}
env_ITS$simpson.g <- Reduce("+", its_simpson.list.g) / length(its_simpson.list.g)

#gini
its_gini.list.g <-  replicate(100, 1:dim(asv_ITS.g)[1], simplify = FALSE)
for (i in 1:1000) {
  its_gini.list.g[[i]] <- apply(as.matrix(rrarefy(asv_ITS.g,sample=170)), 1, function(x) Gini(x))
}
env_ITS$gini.g <- Reduce("+", its_gini.list.g) / length(its_gini.list.g)

#combine at order level
asv_ITS.o <- matrix(0, nrow=nrow(asv_ITS), ncol=length(unique(taxa_ITS$Order)))
rownames(asv_ITS.o) <- rownames(asv_ITS)
colnames(asv_ITS.o) <- unique(taxa_ITS$Order)
for (i in 1:length(unique(taxa_ITS$Order))) {
  temp <- taxa_ITS[which(taxa_ITS$Order == unique(taxa_ITS$Order)[i]),]
  temp2 <- asv_ITS[, which(colnames(asv_ITS) %in% temp$asv), drop=FALSE]
  asv_ITS.o[,i] <- rowSums(temp2)
}
asv_ITS.o <- as.data.frame(asv_ITS.o)


#combine at phylum level
asv_ITS.p <- matrix(0, nrow=nrow(asv_ITS), ncol=length(unique(taxa_ITS$Phylum)))
rownames(asv_ITS.p) <- rownames(asv_ITS)
colnames(asv_ITS.p) <- unique(taxa_ITS$Phylum)
for (i in 1:length(unique(taxa_ITS$Phylum))) {
  temp <- taxa_ITS[which(taxa_ITS$Phylum == unique(taxa_ITS$Phylum)[i]),]
  temp2 <- asv_ITS[, which(colnames(asv_ITS) %in% temp$asv), drop=FALSE]
  asv_ITS.p[,i] <- rowSums(temp2)
}
asv_ITS.p <- as.data.frame(asv_ITS.p)

#pivot for graphs, add site

#species
asv_ITS.s_long <- asv_ITS.s %>%
  mutate(Site_ID = env_ITS$Site_ID) %>% #add site ID to samples
pivot_longer(
    cols = c(1:712), #pick columns to pivot
    names_to = "species", #name column to put original column names in
    values_to = "count") #name column to put values in

#genus

#order

#phylum
```

#### 2023

```{r load Kimpton SOM data, eval=FALSE}

#read in field soil C/N data
SOM_Kimpton <- read_csv("SOM_Kimpton.csv") 

#Combine SOM, POM, and MAOM as one observation per plot
SOM <- SOM_Kimpton %>%
  filter(Fraction == "SOM") %>%
  rename("SOM_C" = "C_gkg") %>%
  rename("SOM_N" = "N_gkg") %>%
  rename("SOM_CN" = "C_N") %>%
  rename("SOM_C_kgm2_7cm" = "C_kgm2_7cm")

POM <- SOM_Kimpton %>%
  filter(Fraction == "POM") %>%
  rename("POM_C" = "C_gkg") %>%
  rename("POM_N" = "N_gkg") %>%
  rename("POM_CN" = "C_N") %>%
  rename("POM_C_kgm2_7cm" = "C_kgm2_7cm")
  
MAOM <- SOM_Kimpton %>%
  filter(Fraction == "MAOM") %>%
  rename("MAOM_C" = "C_gkg") %>%
  rename("MAOM_N" = "N_gkg") %>%
  rename("MAOM_CN" = "C_N") %>%
  rename("MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm" = "C_kgm2_7cm")

SOM_Kimpton2 <- merge(MAOM,POM, by=c("Sample_year", "Site", "Site_ID", "Mgmt_year", "Plot_ID"), all.y=TRUE) %>%
  merge(SOM, by=c("Sample_year", "Site", "Site_ID", "Mgmt_year", "Plot_ID"), all.y=TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_year, Site_ID, Site, Mgmt_year, 
                SOM_C, SOM_N, SOM_CN, POM_C, POM_N, POM_CN, MAOM_C, MAOM_N, MAOM_CN,
                C_gcm3, C_Tha, SOM_C_kgm2_7cm, POM_C_kgm2_7cm, MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm) %>%
  mutate(fMAOM_C = MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm / (POM_C_kgm2_7cm + MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm)) %>% #calculate fMAOM C
  mutate(fMAOM_C_2 = MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm / SOM_C_kgm2_7cm) %>% #calculate fMAOM C
  mutate(fMAOM_N = MAOM_N / (POM_N + MAOM_N)) %>% #calculate fMAOM N
  mutate(fMAOM_N_2 = MAOM_N / SOM_N) #calculate fMAOM N

#remove SOM, POM, and MAOM dataframes to clean up environment
rm(SOM, POM, MAOM)

#summarize SOM data for plots
summary_SOM_Kimpton <- SOM_Kimpton2 %>%
  group_by(Sample_year, Site, Site_ID, Mgmt_year) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#order variables
SOM_Kimpton$Site <- factor(SOM_Kimpton$Site, levels = order_sites)
SOM_Kimpton2$Site <- factor(SOM_Kimpton2$Site, levels = order_sites)
summary_SOM_Kimpton$Site <- factor(summary_SOM_Kimpton$Site, levels = order_sites)

```

```{r load SOM-13C data, warning=FALSE}
  mutate(AM_mm_g = HLD_T0$AM_mm_g[match(SOM_13C_T0$Plot_ID, HLD_T0$Pot)]) %>%
  mutate(other_mm_g = HLD_T0$other_mm_g[match(SOM_13C_T0$Plot_ID, HLD_T0$Pot)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_biomass_gkg = HLD_T0$AM_biomass_gkg[match(SOM_13C_T0$Plot_ID, HLD_T0$Pot)]) %>%
  mutate(total_fun_gkg = HLD_T0$total_fun_gkg[match(SOM_13C_T0$Plot_ID, HLD_T0$Pot)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_C_mgkg = HLD_T0$AM_C_mgkg[match(SOM_13C_T0$Plot_ID, HLD_T0$Pot)]) %>%
  mutate(otherfun_C_mgkg = HLD_T0$otherfun_C_mgkg[match(SOM_13C_T0$Plot_ID, HLD_T0$Pot)]) %>%
  mutate(total_fun_C_mgkg = HLD_T0$total_fun_C_mgkg[match(SOM_13C_T0$Plot_ID, HLD_T0$Pot)]) %>%
  mutate(fun_C_soil_C = ((total_fun_C_mgkg/1000)/SOM_C)*100) %>%
  mutate(fun_C_POM_C = ((total_fun_C_mgkg/1000)/POM_C)*100) %>%
  mutate(pH = SOM_13C_T0$pH <- site_data$pH[match(SOM_13C_T0$Plot_ID, site_data$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(pH_range = case_when(pH <= 5 ~ "Very Strongly Acidic",
                                pH > 5 & pH <= 5.5 ~ "Strongly Acidic",
                                pH > 5.5 & pH <= 6 ~ "Moderately Acidic",
                                pH > 6 & pH <= 6.5 ~ "Mildly Acidic",
                                pH > 6.5 & pH <= 7.3 ~ "Neutral",
                                pH > 7.3 ~ "Alkaline"))

SOM_13C_T6 <- SOM_13C %>%
  filter(Incubation_T == 6) #filter 6 mos
SOM_13C_T6 <- SOM_13C_T6 %>% #add fungi and pH
  mutate(spores_g = HLD_T6$spores_g[match(SOM_13C_T6$Plot_ID, HLD_T6$Pot)]) %>%
```

#### 2026

```{r load 2026 SOM data, warning=FALSE}

#read in field soil C/N data from 2026 and calculate additional
SOM_2026 <- read_csv("SOM_2026.csv") %>%
  rename("SOM_C_kgm2_7cm" = "C_kgm2_7cm") %>%
  mutate(MAOM_perC = 
           MAOM53_perC*(per_53/(per_53+per_45)) + MAOM45_perC*(per_45/(per_53+per_45))) %>% #calculate total MAOM per C
  mutate(MAOM_perN = 
           MAOM53_perN*(per_53/(per_53+per_45)) + MAOM45_perN*(per_45/(per_53+per_45))) %>% #calculate total MAOM per N
  mutate(MAOM_CN = MAOM_perC / MAOM_perN) %>% #calculate total MAOM C/N
  mutate(MAOM45_C_kgm2_7cm = ((MAOM45_perC/100) * per_45 * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>% #calculate MAOM45 C per km2 to 7cm depth
  mutate(MAOM53_C_kgm2_7cm = ((MAOM53_perC/100) * per_53 * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>% #calculate MAOM53 C per km2 to 7cm depth
  mutate(MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm = ((MAOM_perC/100) * per_MAOM * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>%
  mutate(POM_C_kgm2_7cm = ((POM_perC/100) * per_POM * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>%
  mutate(POM53_perC = 
           POM_perC*(per_POM/(per_53+per_POM)) + MAOM53_perC*(per_53/(per_53+per_POM))) %>% #calculate POM C including the <53>45 um fraction
  mutate(per_POM53 = per_POM + per_53) %>% #calculate percentage of POM including the <53>45 um fraction
  mutate(POM53_C_kgm2_7cm = ((POM53_perC/100) * per_POM53 * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>%
  mutate(fMAOM_C = MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm / (POM_C_kgm2_7cm + MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm)) #calculate fMAOM C

#summarize SOM 2026 data 
summary_SOM_2026 <- SOM_2026[c(3:8,10,14,26,29,30:32,35:57)] %>%
  group_by(Site_ID, Site, Mgmt_year, Mgmt_time, Management) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), summary_stats)) #run all summary stats

#combine with above data
SOM_multiyr <- SOM_13C_T0 %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_year, Site, Site_ID, Mgmt_year, pH, SOM_perC, SOM_perN, SOM_CN, SOM_C_kgm2_7cm, POM_perC, POM_perN, POM_C_kgm2_7cm, MAOM_perC, MAOM_perN, MAOM_C_kgm2_7cm, fMAOM_C) %>%
  bind_rows(SOM_2026) 

  

SOM_2026$Site <- factor(SOM_2026$Site, levels = order_sites)
SOM_2026$Site_ID <- factor(SOM_2026$Site_ID, levels = order_IDs)
SOM_multiyr$Site <- factor(SOM_multiyr$Site, levels = order_sites)
SOM_multiyr$Site_ID <- factor(SOM_multiyr$Site_ID, levels = order_IDs)

```

```{r load UK data, warning=FALSE}
#load dataset UK grasslands - from DRYAD repository, Manning et al. 2016
UK_soil <- read_csv("Manning2015_dryad.csv") %>%
  filter(type == "U") %>% #use only unimproved sites
  mutate(POM_C = C250 + C50_250) %>% #match to Wigan data
  mutate(MAOM_C = C50_0.45) %>% #match to Wigan data
  rename("pH" = "PH") %>% #match case with Wigan data
  mutate(vegetation = str_replace(vegetation, "wet grassland", "Wet Grassland")) %>% #match naming with Wigan data
  mutate(vegetation = str_replace(vegetation, "Acid grass", "Acid Grass")) %>% #match naming with Wigan data
  mutate(Sample_year = 2005) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_year, vegetation, type, site, pH, TotalC, POM_C, MAOM_C) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(pH, TotalC, POM_C, MAOM_C), as.numeric) %>%
  na.omit() #only include complete


summary_UKsoils <- UK_soil %>%
  group_by(vegetation) %>%
  summarise(across(pH:MAOM_C, list(mean = ~ mean(., na.rm=TRUE),
                                 sd = ~ sd(., na.rm=TRUE),
                                 se = ~ std.error(., na.rm=TRUE))))


soilC_compare <- SOM_2026 %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_year, Site_ID, SOM_C_kgm2_7cm, POM53_C_kgm2_7cm, MAOM45_C_kgm2_7cm, pH) %>%
  rename("site" = "Site_ID") %>%
  rename("TotalC" = "SOM_C_kgm2_7cm") %>%
  rename("POM_C" = "POM53_C_kgm2_7cm") %>%
  rename("MAOM_C" = "MAOM45_C_kgm2_7cm") %>%
  mutate(type = "R") %>% #R for restored
  mutate(vegetation = case_when(site == "BU" ~ "BU Wet Grassland", #set value in new column 
															  site == "BM" ~ "BM Wet Grassland", 
															  site == "AU" ~ "AU Mesotrophic", 
															  site == "AM" ~ "AM Mesotrophic",
															  site == "FU" ~ "FU Mesotrophic",
															  site == "FM" ~ "FM Mesotrophic")) %>% 
  bind_rows(UK_soil) %>%
  mutate(pH_range = case_when(pH <= 5 ~ "Very Strongly Acidic", #make pH categories
                                pH > 5 & pH <= 5.5 ~ "Strongly Acidic",
                                pH > 5.5 & pH <= 6 ~ "Moderately Acidic",
                                pH > 6 & pH <= 6.5 ~ "Mildly Acidic",
                                pH > 6.5 & pH <= 7.3 ~ "Neutral",
                                pH > 7.3 ~ "Alkaline"))
```

### Incubation biomass decomposition

```{r load incubation biomass data}

#read in incubation data, add beginning, calculate change in biomass
endbiomass <- read_csv("End_incubation_biomass.csv") %>% #load
  mutate(est_beg_drymass = total_pots$root[match(Pot, total_pots$pot)]) %>% #add estimated beginning biomass
  mutate(beg_drymass_perL = est_beg_drymass / 6.1) %>% #calculate dry mass per liter
  mutate(dmass_dT = est_beg_drymass - end_drymass_clean) %>% #calculate change in dry mass
  mutate(dmass_dT_perL = beg_drymass_perL - end_drymass_perL_clean) %>% #calculate change in dry mass per liter
  mutate(decomp_per_unadj = dmass_dT / est_beg_drymass) %>% #calculate decomposition percentage - not adjusting volume
  mutate(decomp_per_adj = dmass_dT_perL / beg_drymass_perL) %>% #calculate decomposition percentage - adjusting volume
  mutate(years =
           case_when(Management == "Unmanaged" ~ 0,
                     Management == "4 Years" ~ 4,
                     Management == "15 Years" ~ 15,
                     Management == "23 Years" ~ 23))

#Add data
endbiomass <- endbiomass %>%
  mutate(AM_hyph_per = AMdata$hyph_percent[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_hyph_ct = AMdata$Hyphae[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_arb_per = AMdata$arbuscule_percent[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_arb_ct = AMdata$Arbuscule[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_ves_ct = AMdata$Vesicle[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(AM_absent = AMdata$Nothing[match(endbiomass$Pot, AMdata$Plot_ID)]) %>%
  mutate(pH = SOM_13C_T0$pH <- site_data$pH[match(endbiomass$Pot, site_data$Plot_ID)]) %>%

                                pH > 6 & pH <= 6.5 ~ "Mildly Acidic",
```

```{r NBN}

#read in downloaded csv from National Biodiversity Network Atlas
NBN <- read_csv("NBNatlas_Wigan.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>%
  dplyr::select(scientific_name, common_name, event_date, month, year, latitude_wgs84, longitude_wgs84, 
                individual_count, abundance, kingdom, phylum, order, class, family, genus)

#convert NBN observations to sf object
NBN_sf <- NBN %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude_wgs84", "latitude_wgs84"), crs = 4326)

#find nearest site for each observation and calculate distance
NBN_sites <- NBN_sf %>%
  mutate(
    nearest_site = st_nearest_feature(., sites_sf),
    Site_ID = sites_sf$Site_ID[nearest_site],
    distance_m = st_distance(., sites_sf[nearest_site, ], by_element = TRUE) %>% 
      as.numeric()
  ) %>%
  filter(distance_m <= 100) %>%  # Filter to 50m threshold
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

### Prediction modeling

#### Set up

```{r predict coal}

#difference function to compare colors
#comparecolor <- function(x) {
#return(sqrt(())
#}


#predictive modeling

#pre-define variables
target <- "coal_per"   # change if different
feature_base <- c("l", "a", "b")
spectral_cols <- names(color_cal) %>% purrr::keep(~ grepl("^\\d+nm$", .x)) #selects columns with nm
predictors <- c(feature_base, spectral_cols, "chroma", "hue") 
group_col    <- "sample_grp" #group by coal_per to keep technical replicates together
cv_type      <- "grouped" #"grouped" (groupKFold) or "logo" (leave-one-group-out by coal_per)



#train control: grouped, but repeated CV as backup if no group
if ("sample_grp" %in% names(color_cal_g1)) {
  idx <- caret::groupKFold(factor(color_cal_g1$sample_grp), k = min(5, length(unique(color_cal_g1$sample_grp))))
  tr_ctrl <- trainControl(method="cv", index = idx, savePredictions="final", summaryFunction = defaultSummary, allowParallel=TRUE)
} else {
  tr_ctrl <- trainControl(method="repeatedcv", number=5, repeats=5, savePredictions="final", summaryFunction = defaultSummary, allowParallel=TRUE)
  message("sample_grp not found; using repeated CV")
}

#set up parallel backend
cl <- makePSOCKcluster(parallel::detectCores() - 1); registerDoParallel(cl); on.exit({ stopCluster(cl); registerDoSEQ() })



```

#### Partial Least Squares Regression setup

```{r pls coal g}

#PLS via caret/pls
set.seed(42)
tic("tuning pls")
pls_fit_g <- train(x = color_cal_g2 %>% #
                   dplyr::select(all_of(predictors)), y = color_cal_g2[[target]],
                 method="pls", preProc=c("center","scale"),
                 tuneLength = min(10, length(predictors)), trControl = tr_ctrl, metric="RMSE")
toc(); print(pls_fit_g)

#PLS final using pls::plsr with the selected ncomp
ncomp_g <- pls_fit_g$bestTune$ncomp #4      RMSE R2 MAE 2.831338  0.9398291  2.669456
pls_formula_g <- as.formula(paste(target, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")))
pls_final_g <- plsr(pls_formula_g, data = color_cal_g2, ncomp = ncomp_g, scale = TRUE, validation = "none")
summary(pls_final_g)

#bootstrap PLS PIs function
bootstrap_pls_pi_g <- function(df_train, unknown_df, formula, ncomp_g, n_boot = 200){
  if (is.null(unknown_df) || nrow(unknown_df)==0) return(NULL)
  preds <- replicate(n_boot, {
    b <- df_train[sample(nrow(df_train), replace=TRUE), ]
    as.numeric(predict(plsr(formula, data=b, ncomp=ncomp_g, scale=TRUE), newdata = unknown_df, ncomp = ncomp_g))
  })
  tibble(pred_pls_g = apply(preds,1,median), pred_pls_lo_g = apply(preds,1,quantile,0.025), pred_pls_hi_g = apply(preds,1,quantile,0.975))
}


```

```{r pls coal s}

#PLS via caret/pls
set.seed(42)
tic("tuning pls")
pls_fit_s <- train(x = color_cal_s %>% #
                   dplyr::select(all_of(predictors)), y = color_cal_s[[target]],
                 method="pls", preProc=c("center","scale"),
                 tuneLength = min(10, length(predictors)), trControl = tr_ctrl, metric="RMSE")
toc(); print(pls_fit_s)

#PLS final using pls::plsr with the selected ncomp
ncomp_s <- pls_fit_s$bestTune$ncomp #3      RMSE R2 MAE 1.065895  0.9893903  0.8936231
pls_formula_s <- as.formula(paste(target, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")))
pls_final_s <- plsr(pls_formula_s, data = color_cal_s, ncomp = ncomp_s, scale = TRUE, validation = "none")
summary(pls_final_s)

#bootstrap PLS PIs function
bootstrap_pls_pi_s <- function(df_train, unknown_df, formula, ncomp_s, n_boot = 200){
  if (is.null(unknown_df) || nrow(unknown_df)==0) return(NULL)
  preds <- replicate(n_boot, {
    b <- df_train[sample(nrow(df_train), replace=TRUE), ]
    as.numeric(predict(plsr(formula, data=b, ncomp=ncomp_s, scale=TRUE), newdata = unknown_df, ncomp = ncomp_s))
  })
  tibble(pred_pls_s = apply(preds,1,median), pred_pls_lo_s = apply(preds,1,quantile,0.025), pred_pls_hi_s = apply(preds,1,quantile,0.975))
}


```

```{r rf coal g}
                      dplyr::select(all_of(predictors)), y = color_cal_g2[[target]],
                    method="ranger", preProc=c("center","scale"),
                    tuneLength = 5, trControl = tr_ctrl, metric="RMSE",
                    num.trees = 1000, importance="permutation", num.threads = 1)
toc()
print(ranger_fit_g)
best_g <- ranger_fit_g$bestTune # mtry 2 extratrees  RMSE R2 MAE 1.361917  0.9779578  1.199282

#prepare scaled data and fit final quantile forest with more trees
scaler_g <- preProcess(color_cal_g2 %>% dplyr::select(all_of(predictors)), method = c("center","scale"))
color_cal_proc_g <- predict(scaler_g, color_cal_g2 %>% dplyr::select(all_of(predictors))); color_cal_proc_g[[target]] <- color_cal_g2[[target]]

r_qrf_g <- ranger::ranger(dependent.variable.name = target, data = color_cal_proc_g,
                        num.trees = 2000, mtry = best_g$mtry,
                        splitrule = if("splitrule" %in% names(best_g)) best_g$splitrule else "variance",
                        min.node.size = if("min.node.size" %in% names(best_g)) best_g$min.node.size else 5,
                        importance = "permutation", quantreg = TRUE, write.forest = TRUE, num.threads = 1)


```

#### Model validation
```{r model predictions vs calibration - pls}

#create df with randomly selected values from calibration data - g
set.seed(42)
val_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(color_cal_g2)), size = floor(nrow(color_cal_g2) * 0.2))

#create splits
df_val <- color_cal_g2[val_idx, ]
df_train <- color_cal_g2[-val_idx, ]

#sizes
cat("Train rows:", nrow(df_train), " | Val rows:", nrow(df_val), "\n") 


#PLS predictions
if (exists("df_val")) { message("Computing PLS bootstrap PIs..."); tic("PLS boot"); 
  pls_val <- bootstrap_pls_pi_g(color_cal_g2, df_val, pls_formula_g, ncomp_g, n_boot=200); toc(); 
if (!is.null(pls_val)) pls_val <- pls_val %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~pmin(pmax(.x,0),100))) }

#add results to df
pls_val_g <- pls_val %>%
  mutate(coal_per = df_val$coal_per)

#compute rmse on prediction vs true coal_per
rmse_vec <- function(true, pred) sqrt(mean((true - pred)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
rmse_pls <- rmse_vec(pls_val_g$coal_per, pls_val_g$pred_pls_g)
rmse_pls #1.7
performance::r2(lm(coal_per ~ pred_pls_g, data=pls_val_g)) #adj R2 0.92
performance::rmse(lm(coal_per ~ pred_pls_g, data=pls_val_g)) #1.59
```

```{r model predictions vs calibration - rf}
#create df with randomly selected values from calibration data
set.seed(42)
val_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(color_cal_g2)), size = floor(nrow(color_cal_g2) * 0.2))

df_train <- color_cal_g2[-val_idx, ]

#RF predictions

if (exists("r_qrf_g")) {

  p_point <- predict(r_qrf_g, data = val_proc, type = "response")$predictions
  p_q  <- predict(r_qrf_g, data = val_proc, type = "quantiles", quantiles = c(0.025, 0.975))$predictions
  rf_val_g <- data.frame(pred_rf_g = pmin(pmax(p_point,0),100), 
           pred_rf_lo_g = pmin(pmax(p_q[,1],0),100), 
           pred_rf_hi_g = pmin(pmax(p_q[,2],0),100)) %>%
    mutate(coal_per = df_val$coal_per)
} else p_point <- p_q <- NULL

#compute rmse on prediction vs true coal_per
rmse_rf <- rmse_vec(rf_val_g$coal_per, rf_val_g$pred_rf_g)
rmse_rf #0.53
performance::r2(lm(coal_per ~ pred_rf_g, data=rf_val_g)) #0.991
performance::rmse(lm(coal_per ~ pred_rf_g, data=rf_val_g)) #0.53

  rf_val <- data.frame(pred_rf = pmin(pmax(p_point,0),100), 
           pred_rf_lo = pmin(pmax(p_q[,1],0),100), 
           pred_rf_hi = pmin(pmax(p_q[,2],0),100)) %>%
    mutate(coal_per = df_val$coal_per)
} else p_point <- p_q <- NULL
```

```{r predict 2023}
#run PLSR on ground samples

  pls_res <- bootstrap_pls_pi_g(color_cal_g2, color_soil23, pls_formula_g, ncomp_g, n_boot=200); toc(); 
if (!is.null(pls_res)) pls_res <- pls_res %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~pmin(pmax(.x,0),100))) }

#add results to df
color_soil23 <- color_soil23 %>%
  cbind(pls_res) 


#RFR predictions - ground
color_proc <- predict(scaler_g, color_soil23 %>% dplyr::select(all_of(predictors))) #scale for RF
if (exists("r_qrf_g")) {
  # ensure val_proc is a data.frame with same column names as used for fitting
  p_point <- predict(r_qrf_g, data = color_proc, type = "response")$predictions
  p_q  <- predict(r_qrf_g, data = color_proc, type = "quantiles", quantiles = c(0.025, 0.975))$predictions
  rf_res <- data.frame(pred_rf = pmin(pmax(p_point,0),100), 
           pred_rf_lo = pmin(pmax(p_q[,1],0),100), 
           pred_rf_hi = pmin(pmax(p_q[,2],0),100)) 
} else p_point <- p_q <- NULL

#add results to df
color_soil23 <- color_soil23 %>%
  cbind(rf_res) 

#calc mean per sample

coal_soil23_means <- color_soil23 %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_grp, site_id, pred_pls_g:pred_rf_hi) %>%
  group_by(sample_grp, site_id) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), mean)) #mean


#calculate percent carbon potentially attributable to coal - use low values for conservative est
per_coal23 <- coal_soil23_means %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_grp, pred_rf) %>%
  rename("Plot_ID" = "sample_grp") %>%
  rename("per_coal" = "pred_rf")

SOM_13C_T0 <- SOM_13C_T0 %>%
  merge(per_coal23, by="Plot_ID", all.x = TRUE) 

SOM_13C_T0 <- SOM_13C_T0 %>%
  mutate(coal_C = (per_coal/100)*65) %>% #percent C coal
  mutate(new_C = SOM_perC - coal_C) #percent C non-coal (assumed new SOC)
```

```{r predict 2026}
  p_point <- predict(r_qrf_g, data = color26_proc, type = "response")$predictions

  rf_res <- data.frame(pred_rf = pmin(pmax(p_point,0),100),

} else p_point <- p_q <- NULL

#calculate percent carbon potentially attributable to coal
SOM_2026 <- SOM_2026 %>%
  mutate(per_coal = coal_soil26_means$pred_rf[match(SOM_2026$Sample_ID, coal_soil26_means$sample_grp)]) %>%
  mutate(coal_C = (per_coal/100)*65) %>% #percent C coal
  mutate(new_C = SOM_perC - coal_C) %>% #percent C non-coal (assumed new SOC)
  mutate(new_C_kgm2_7cm = ((new_C/100) * adj_BD * (10/1000) * 10000 * 0.7)) %>% #calculate C per km2 to 7cm depth
  mutate(fracC_coal = coal_C / (coal_C + new_C)) %>%
  mutate(fracC_new = new_C / (coal_C + new_C))
```

## Correlations
```{r corr 2023}

#2023

#make numeric, remove irrelevant
SOM_13C_T0_num <- SOM_13C_T0 %>% 
  dplyr::select(SOM_C, SOM_N, SOM_CN, POM_C, POM_N, POM_CN, MAOM_C, MAOM_N, MAOM_CN, SOM_15N, 
                g_debris, pH,
                root_mass, shoot_mass, plant_r, plant_shannon, plant_simpson,
                AM_hyph_per, AM_arb_per) %>%
  cbind(soil_metals_wide) %>%
  dplyr::select_if(is.numeric)


#df
df_corr23 <- round(cor(SOM_13C_T0_num, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method="pearson"), 3) #create df for corr. matrix, will use only complete pairs (ignore other NAs), w/3 decimals
df_corr23 #view correlations


#test significance P values with 95% confidence interval
cortest23 <- cor.mtest(SOM_13C_T0_num, conf.level = 0.95)
cortest23 #view P values

#plot matrix with corrplot
corrplot::corrplot(df_corr23, method = 'circle', type = 'upper', #plot upper half, show as colors
         col = colors_ramp2, #set gradient colors from defined palette in Chunk 3
         mar=c(1,0,1,0), #set margins for all incl. title - BLTR
         tl.col = 'black',tl.cex = 0.4, #text label color, size
         tl.srt = 90, tl.offset = 0.4, #text label angle rotation, offset
         order = 'alphabet',  #FPC first principal component order
         p.mat = cortest23$p, #define p values
         insig = 'label_sig', #add *s for significance levels
         sig.level = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05), #define significance levels
         pch.cex = 0.3, #star sizes
         cl.cex = 0.5, #color legend text size
         cex.main = 1, #set title font size
         title = "Correlation Matrix" #set title
         )


```

```{r corr 2026}

#2023

SOM_2026_num <- SOM_2026 %>%
```

```{r soil char}
#soil pH differences - 2023 data
shapiro.test(resid(lm(pH ~ Management, data = site_data))) #check normality of residuals - not normal
kruskal.test(pH ~ Management, data = site_data) #Kruskal-Wallis test - significant
dunn.test(site_data$pH, site_data$Management, method = "bonferroni", kw=TRUE) #23 yr vs. 4 and 0, 15 vs. 4

#soil bulk density differences - 2026 data
shapiro.test(resid(lm(adj_BD ~ Management * Site, data = SOM_2026))) #check normality of residuals - normal
summary(aov(adj_BD ~ Management * Site, data = SOM_2026)) #ANOVA - none significant
```

```{r SOC chart - Kimpton, eval=FALSE}

#SOM C bar chart with error bars
ggplot(data = summary_SOM_Kimpton, aes(x=Site, y=SOM_C_mean, fill=Site)) + 
	geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.7, position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=colors4) + #define colors to use
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=SOM_C_mean-SOM_C_se, ymax=SOM_C_mean+SOM_C_se),
  color = "grey10", width = 0.7, position = "dodge") + 
  ggtitle("Soil Organic Matter C per site") + #add a graph title
  xlab("Site") + ylab("C (g/kg)") + #define/change X and Y labels
  my_theme

#save figure
ggsave('SOC_Kimpton.svg', #save plot name and type - can be "eps", "pdf", "jpeg", "tiff", "png", "bmp", "svg"
	path = "Figures", #save to folder within working directory
	width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", #set dimensions for figure
	dpi = 300, #set resolution
	bg=NULL) #background from plot specifications

```

